inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, $69,213k). No PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag exists for NVR -- awards are mostly options settled by cash exercise (proceeds $80.1M FY2025), so there is no net-share-settlement withholding to add; SBC incl. equity taxes equals the add-back.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 2,664,860 cover-page shares at 2026-07-31 (Q2 2026 10-Q, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) + 118,661 dilutive option increment from the Q2 2026 EPS table = 2,783,521. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. NVR is a heavy repurchaser ($1,833M FY2025, $1,006M H1 2026; count down from 6.1M in 2010 to 2.7M), so the flat count is more than funded; buybacks beyond the SBC offset are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.1%, ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.1 (NVR's 5y beta vs S&P sits 1.0-1.2) -> cost of equity ~9.6%; the $908M of 3.0% senior notes due 2030 are ~5% of capital, giving WACC ~9.5%. Housing cyclicality and rate sensitivity are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight -- not stacked into WACC, and WACC is identical across the three scenarios (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost (offices, model homes) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA/EBIT, so no separate lease line is charged and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment, consistently applied. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- NVR has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: EBITDA in core_metrics was derived as pretax income + homebuilding interest expense - homebuilding other income (which is almost entirely interest on the cash pile), so the forward flows exclude interest income by construction, and FY2025 interest income of $96.3M is stripped from the owner-FCF anchor. Net cash ($236.5M at 2026-06-30) is added once in the bridge. Net cash is now below 1x the FCF base because $2.8B of buybacks since end-FY2024 ran down the pile, which is exactly why the FY2025 interest income must not be carried forward.
inputs.mortgage_banking_note: NVR Mortgage Finance funds loans held for sale with a repurchase facility secured by those loans; it is excluded from total_debt (senior notes only, consistent with the Metrics CSV) and treated as working capital of the segment. Mortgage banking pretax (~3% of revenue, 5-6% of profit) is inside the consolidated EBITDA margin.
inputs.timing_note: Year 1 is FY2026 (Dec year-end), three-quarters elapsed at the valuation date, while the balance sheet is at 2026-06-30. H1 2026 owner FCF (~$100M after SBC and interest income, ~$35/share) is therefore counted both in net cash and in the year-1 flow; the one-period discounting of FY2026 roughly offsets it. Immaterial relative to the scenario spread.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner-fcf.md + the cyclical adaptations), 10-year explicit horizon because margins are being normalised from a FY2026 trough, not carried forward. NVR is a US homebuilder -- an operating cyclical with no banking, REIT or holdco features -- so the routing table sends it to the owner-FCF engine; the mid-cycle treatment lives in the margin paths (FY2026 ~14% EBITDA margin recovering to 14.5% base / 16.5% bull / 12% bear) rather than in a mid-cycle FCF override, because the component build already anchors to FY2025 actuals and the FY2026 run-rate. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry existed. Reported FCF for FY2025 is OCF $1,121.3M less capex $24.5M = $1,096.8M; owner FCF = 1,096.8 - 69.2 SBC - 96.3 interest income = $931.3M (9.0% of revenue).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle revenue growth. revenue_5yr_cagr (6.5%) haircut for the FY2026 contraction and the permitting bottleneck on community count; equity CAGR is distorted by buybacks exceeding earnings and EPS CAGR by the shrinking share count, so neither is a usable growth anchor for NVR.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.5% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 13.7% and revenue 6.5%: >30% divergence. NVR retires nearly all earnings via buybacks (FY2024 buybacks $2,058M vs net income $1,682M), so book value barely grows while per-share EPS compounds; the equity CAGR is a capital-allocation artefact, not a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on the SBC- and interest-income-adjusted series. 3-year CAGRs (-0.65% revenue, -18.7% owner FCF) run from the FY2022 house-price peak (21.6% EBITDA margin) to FY2025 (16.6%) and describe the down-leg of a cycle, not a trend. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-18.7%) is worse than the reported (-16.0%) mainly because interest income on the 2023-24 cash pile was flattering reported FCF; that stream is now shrinking with the cash.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -8%: H1 2026 revenue -15.9% YoY, but Q2 new orders +9% and backlog +9% in units at -5% price point to H2 settlements roughly flat YoY (consensus FY2026 EPS ~$367, -16%). FY2027 flat with mortgage rates still ~6.3-6.5% and the price reset flowing through; FY2028-30 4-5% as rates ease toward ~6% and the 184,400 controlled lots (+76% since 2019) convert to communities as permitting clears; fading to 2.5% nominal (household formation + inflation) by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin (ex interest income) was 10.7-12.5% in FY2013-16, 13.8-14.9% in FY2017-20, 18.5-21.6% at the FY2021-22 house-price peak, 19.2% FY2023-24 and 16.6% FY2025; H1 2026 ran ~13.3% (homebuilding gross margin 19.2% vs 21.5%, $21.7M lot-deposit impairments, SG&A deleverage). Base takes FY2026 at 14.0% with a stronger H2, a 13.5% FY2027 trough as price concessions annualise, then recovery to a 14.5% mid-cycle: the FY2017-25 average ex the two peak years, and above the pre-2017 range because scale and the land-light model have improved structurally.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC was 0.67% of revenue FY2025 and 0.77% H1 2026 (fixed-dollar option grants over a smaller revenue base); held at 0.75% -- it is a rounding line for NVR.
base.capex_da_rationale: NVR owns almost no land or plant: D&A 0.24% and capex 0.24% of FY2025 revenue (24.5M each). Capex set a touch above D&A for production-facility renewals.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes $438.8M on ~$1,762M pretax = 24.9%; GAAP provision 24.0%. 24.5% held flat -- no NOLs, no valuation-allowance noise, federal 21% + state.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: growth consumes cash through lot deposits and homes under construction (OCF ran $220-310M below net income in FY2024-25 as controlled lots grew). -10% of the revenue change is below the recent 2-3%-of-revenue consumption because that included a deliberate counter-cyclical lot-pipeline build; a revenue decline in FY2026 releases a modest amount.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x; NVR has earned the top of it with 40%+ ROE and net cash). Gordon at 9.5%/2.5% = 14.6x, so Gordon binds and the cap is a brake only.
base.narrative: Rates grind down to ~6% by 2028, affordability repairs slowly, NVR holds share with its build-to-order model, community count catches up to the lot pipeline, and margins settle at a 14.5% mid-cycle well below the 2021-24 house-price-inflation peak.

bull.narrative: Mortgage rates fall to the high-5s by 2027, the ~500k-unit shortfall of sub-$260k homes pulls Ryan Homes entry-level demand forward, permitting clears so the 184k controlled lots convert to community-count growth, and the land-light model recaptures a 16.5% EBITDA margin -- the FY2017-25 average including the peak years, still short of FY2023-24's 19%. Revenue compounds 8% through FY2028-29 and the buyback keeps shrinking the count.

bear.narrative: Rates re-tighten into 2027 and a labour-market downturn lifts cancellations; spec-heavy national builders (DHI, LEN, PHM) discount finished inventory that build-to-order NVR cannot match, so volume and price both give way (FY2026 -12%, FY2027 -8%). Further lot-deposit impairments follow the Q2 2026 $21.7M. Margins trough at 11% -- the FY2013-16 range -- and recover only to 12% as community count stays bottlenecked. No solvency question: net cash, no land book, 3% notes due 2030; the bear is an earnings-power case, not a survival case.

scenario_narratives.base: Rates ease toward 6% by 2028; FY2026 revenue -8% and EBITDA margin 14%, a 13.5% trough in FY2027, then 4-5% growth as the lot pipeline converts and a 14.5% mid-cycle margin -- below the 2021-24 house-price-inflation years, above the pre-2017 range.
scenario_narratives.bull: High-5s mortgage rates by 2027 plus permitting relief unlock the 184k controlled lots; entry-level shortage drives 8% growth in FY2028-29 and margins recapture 16.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates re-tighten and spec-builder discounting takes share from build-to-order NVR; two down years, 11% trough margin recovering only to 12%; earnings-power case, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: homebuilding is a rate-driven cyclical in the early part of a down-leg (H1 2026 revenue -16%, margin compressing, consensus still being cut as of late September), and a re-tightening of rates or a labour-market turn would extend it -- though the bear is an earnings case with no balance-sheet risk, which is why it is not higher. Bull down to 25%: it needs three independent things -- rates falling to the high-5s, municipal permitting clearing so community count catches the lot pipeline, and margins recapturing 16.5% without the house-price inflation that produced the 2021-24 margins.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NVR is valued as an operating cyclical on owner FCF: SBC expensed, interest income on the (now much smaller) cash pile stripped and the net cash added once, the share count held flat, and cyclicality handled by normalising the EBITDA margin from the FY2026 trough across three explicit paths rather than by a WACC premium. The capital-light lot-option model makes owner FCF track net income closely (capex and D&A are ~0.25% of revenue), so the valuation is essentially a question of what mid-cycle margin and growth the market should capitalise -- and at the current price the market is paying for something closer to the bull margin path than the base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is worth roughly 7-8% of base value; the 14.5% base sits between the 12.9% pre-2017 average and the 16.9% post-2017 average.
Mortgage-rate path drives both volume and price; the scenarios span high-5s to a re-tightening but a 2008-style credit event is outside all three.
Community-count bottleneck: controlled lots are up 76% since 2019 but active communities are flat; if permitting does not clear, the FY2028-30 growth in base does not arrive.
Lot-deposit impairments scale with price declines ($21.7M in Q2 2026); a sharper price reset would add to the bear case.

Flat share count understates the per-share compounding NVR has delivered historically; buybacks executed below intrinsic value add value the model does not credit (and above it, destroy value it does not debit).
